title: Kali Reproducibility Signoff Foundation
goal: Make the supported local/Kali host path reproducible as an explicit signoff lane instead of relying on ad hoc live-host checks.
scope: Define and validate the first install/update/restart/signoff packet for the supported local host path, including service health, static asset freshness, browser-visible app loading, report export, and one safe smoke run. Reuse existing host scripts and acceptance harnesses.
generation_reason: Backlog refresh requested by the project owner after the previous queue ended at backlog item 10.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement this task until it is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Stay limited to reproducibility, health, asset freshness, and safe smoke validation. Do not redesign deployment or add hosted multi-tenancy.
notes: Use local, authorized, or fixture-backed targets only.
Do not run uncontrolled external scanning.

success_criteria: A documented Kali/local-host signoff procedure exists and matches the repo scripts.
The procedure verifies health, static app load, report export, and at least one safe smoke path.
Stale asset and stale service failure modes are called out honestly.
Validation evidence is recorded under the accepted repo result paths.
No hosted deployment or multi-tenant architecture is introduced.

acceptance_criteria: The signoff procedure is reproducible from repo scripts.
The safe smoke run produces evidence without probing the control plane as the target.
The docs state what was not validated.

before_promotion: The prior active task is completed and logged.
The host path is still a supported deployment lane.
after_completion: Update DONE_LOG.md with the host reproducibility evidence.
Update CURRENT_STATE.md with the reproducibility baseline and remaining host risks.
Promote exactly one next approved task package into NEXT_TASK.md, or set an explicit holding state if the queue is exhausted.
